bullets.title: Semis/Optical broadly down 5-7% premarket on FN miss and rate shock
bullets.body: Multiple semiconductor and optical names sold off sharply in premarket: MRVL -6.5%, COHR -6.8%, LITE -6.6%, WDC -6.7%, ALAB -5%, CRWV -4%, STX -6.3%, MU down notably. FN (Fabrinet) dropped 12.6% on an earnings miss despite analyst commentary that the 28% consensus FY27 growth estimate appears too low (CEO indicated 40%+ growth is achievable; $12.5-14B revenue target in 12-24 months). SOXX index down ~3.5%. Klarna's 3Q guide of $940-980M vs $1.11B consensus also weighed on AFRM (-4.1% in sympathy).

bullets.title: MRVL: TD Cowen raises PT to $225 from $200 despite premarket weakness
bullets.body: TD Cowen raised its Marvell Technology price target to $225 from $200. The PT raise comes as MRVL trades down ~6.5% in premarket amid the broader semiconductor selloff. Wolfe Research is also hosting a webcast Aug 21 covering AI implications for NVDA, AVGO, and MRVL earnings.

bullets.title: FSLR: Morgan Stanley raises PT to $323 from $245 on Section 232 tariff tailwind
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised its First Solar price target to $323 from $245, citing a bullish outcome from Section 232 tariffs. MS forecasts $0.375/W ASP in 2029 and $0.385/W in 2030. FSLR is trading +1% premarket as a limited gainer amid the broader tech selloff.

bullets.title: META: Trial over youth mental health harm begins; penalty risk up to $1.4T
bullets.body: A 29-state trial against Meta over alleged harm to children from social media begins today in California, with potential penalties cited as high as $1.4T. Citi notes an Australia-style under-16 ban is unlikely near-term given legislative timelines. Instagram separately announced a logo refresh after 10 years. META is trading roughly flat in premarket per Morgan Stanley's internet note.

bullets.title: GOOGL/AMZN/META: Morgan Stanley Internet — AI ROIC debate drags names lower
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Internet team flagged AMZN down 4% and GOOGL down 2% as the AI ROIC debate weighs on sector valuations. AMZN/GOOGL/META now trade at 20x/17x/19x 2026E EPS, down 35%/35%/19% vs. TTM averages. APP fell 9%, BKNG -1%, UBER +1%. MS maintains Attractive industry view. Separately, Hedgeye is building AMZN and MSFT positions on dips as both return to bullish trend.

bullets.title: GOOGL, META, DASH, CVNA, ABNB: Citi July traffic trends broadly positive
bullets.body: Citi's July internet traffic tracker shows GOOGL Search share +10bps M/M globally to 91.3%; META Instagram U.S. time spent/DAU +13% Y/Y to 61 mins with downloads up 3 spots to #6; DASH U.S. MAUs +10% Y/Y; CVNA web traffic +62% Y/Y; ABNB downloads +33% Y/Y; BKNG global MAUs +6% Y/Y. RDDT U.S. visit growth slowed to +1% Y/Y. META core apps (FB/IG/WA) U.S. MAUs declined 3.5% Y/Y. Citi's top picks remain AMZN, GOOGL, DASH, CVNA, RDDT.

bullets.title: AMZN: Louisiana data center investment expanded from $12B to $18B
bullets.body: Amazon is growing its Louisiana data center investment from $12B (committed in February) to $18B, adding a third campus in Shreveport spanning Caddo and Bossier Parishes in partnership with STACK Infrastructure.

bullets.title: NFLX: Roth tracking ad tier, password crackdown, and new content monetization
bullets.body: Roth QSG is running a proprietary survey on Netflix's ad-supported tier (raised to $8.99/month from $7.99), password crackdown elasticity, and new content drivers including WWE, NFL, MLB live programming, video podcasts via Spotify, and interactive games. Results will track plan mix, churn, and switching across major streaming platforms.

bullets.title: RCL: Hedgeye raises to Best Idea List on yield re-acceleration and new ship optionality
bullets.body: Hedgeye moved RCL higher on its Best Idea List with added conviction, citing new ship launches (2 river cruise ships in 2027, 4 in 2028+), private destination/beach club revenue, growing direct booking mix via AI referral search, and industry-best cost containment. Q3 data expected to provide good visibility into Q4 pricing pace and 1H 2027 outlook.

bullets.title: DUOL: DA Davidson upgrades to Buy; DAU tracking 24% YoY, 200bps margin upside vs. consensus
bullets.body: DA Davidson upgraded Duolingo to Buy with a $160 PT (17x 2027 EBITDA), citing Q3 DAU tracking at 24.0% YoY growth (vs. 23.1% in Q2) and re-acceleration expected in 2027 from extended free trials, new subscription plans, and reworked ads. Davidson models 200bps margin expansion in 2027 vs. consensus +40bps.

bullets.title: CRM: Checks modestly improved with Agentforce traction; Tableau/Marketing Cloud remain weak
bullets.body: Citi's channel checks on Salesforce improved modestly with positive Agentforce deployment data and pricing/packaging tailwinds. However, Tableau and Marketing Cloud remain weak spots. RDDT is separately experimenting with AI-voice audio/video format conversion.

bullets.title: NBIS: Vineland Phase 2 approval removes key risk; DA Davidson raises PT to $250
bullets.body: The Vineland Planning Board approved Phase 2 of a data center campus with Nebius as tenant using Bloom Energy fuel cells. DA Davidson raised its NBIS PT to $250 (Neutral), noting it now trades at a premium to CRWV after the approval removes a significant risk overhang.

bullets.title: NOK: Jefferies bullish on medium-term guidance upside despite near-term capacity risk
bullets.body: Jefferies sees significant upside to Nokia's 6-8% CAGR Network Infrastructure guidance through 2028, modeling 18% growth instead. New InP fab capacity coming online Q4 2026 is unlikely to contribute meaningfully to 2026 results, but near-term upside is available via switching/IP networks sourced from Broadcom and TSMC. NOK management characterized medium-term guidance as very conservative with scope to raise 2027-2028 targets.

bullets.title: BABA: Reports Q1 earnings 8/20; options imply ~6.9% move; stock +7.5% since May
bullets.body: Alibaba is scheduled to report Q1 earnings on August 20. Consensus expects CNY268.48B revenue, CNY36.70B adjusted EBITDA (13.7% margin), and CNY10.14 non-GAAP EPADS. Cloud Intelligence Group revenue estimate CNY47.30B. Near-term options imply ~6.9% post-earnings move; BABA has beaten EPS consensus 13 of 20 quarters. Stock +7.5% since May 12 vs. S&P 500 +4.6%. Premarket BABA is +5% on new Alipay merchant platform launch.

bullets.title: ROST: Q2 consensus expects 7.7% comps and $1.94 EPS; Goldman sees traffic leading off-price peers
bullets.body: Ross Stores Q2 consensus is at $1.94 EPS (vs. $1.85-1.93 guidance) and +7.7% comps (vs. +6-7% guidance). Goldman's off-price tracker shows ROST with the strongest traffic and transaction momentum in the sector, while TJX moderates and BURL remains muted. Options imply ~7.1% post-earnings move.

bullets.title: COHR/FN: Optical transceiver supply chain under dual pressure — FCC ban risk and China InP retaliation
bullets.body: 22V Research flags FCC moving toward banning Chinese optical transceiver imports by year-end, while Beijing is signaling retaliatory export restrictions on indium phosphide, a critical substrate for high-speed lasers used in U.S. data center buildout. This creates a dual supply chain risk for optical component names including COHR. The U.S.-China tech truce expires November 10.

bullets.title: TSMC: Korean media reports A16 process secures backside power delivery edge over Intel, Samsung
bullets.body: Korean media reports TSMC has validated A16, the industry's first angstrom-class CMOS process with backside power delivery, putting it ahead of Intel and Samsung in next-generation semiconductor manufacturing.

bullets.title: UBER: AV disruption risk overstated; Pony.ai expanding 2,000+ robotaxi fleet across Europe
bullets.body: Jefferies/Klein argues UBER's autonomous vehicle disruption risk is overstated, calling Waymo competition a long-duration threat not a near-term earnings risk. A diversified AV supplier ecosystem is emerging (Pony.ai with 2,000+ European robotaxis, WeRide in Middle East) that would strengthen rather than disintermediate the UBER platform. WeRide guided recovery to 15-20 orders/vehicle/day in Q4 with ~800 vehicles.

bullets.title: INTC/HPE/DELL: Citi bullish on AI hardware cycle ahead of earnings; prefers enterprise OEMs
bullets.body: Citi's 2Q hardware and storage preview flags elevated earnings expectations driven by AI-led infrastructure demand, improving enterprise storage pricing, and constructive supply chain commentary. Citi prefers enterprise OEMs (HPE, DELL) with AI/enterprise server and networking exposure. Premarket: INTC, COHR, WDC, LITE, STX all down 5-7%.

bullets.title: ROKU: At 52-week high, +75.7% YTD per StreetAccount breadth scan
bullets.body: ROKU hit a 52-week high at $158.60 (+0.2% on the day) with a YTD gain of +75.7%, appearing in StreetAccount's 52-week high list with the Health Technology sector leading high counts at 20 stocks.
